text: Correctly stated: for primary primes π₁, π₂ of ℤ[ω] with different norms, the cubic residue symbols (π₁/π₂)₃ and (π₂/π₁)₃ are equal (Ireland–Rosen, *A Classical Introduction to Modern Number Theory*, Ch. 9 §3); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: an even unimodular lattice has rank divisible by 8, and its theta series is a modular form of weight rank/2 for SL₂(ℤ) (Serre, *A Course in Arithmetic*, VII §6); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.
Correctly stated: the Suzuki group Sz(q) is simple for every q = 2^{2m+1} with m ≥ 1 (Wilson, *The Finite Simple Groups*, §4.2); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: if |Σ aᵢⱼ sᵢ tⱼ| ≤ C for all scalars of modulus at most 1, then |Σ aᵢⱼ⟨uᵢ, vⱼ⟩| ≤ K·C for unit vectors in any Hilbert space, with K = 8 real and 16 complex, not sharp (Albiac–Kalton, *Topics in Banach Space Theory*, §8.1); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: for a semisimple Lie algebra 𝔤 over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero with Cartan subalgebra 𝔥, restriction identifies the invariants S(𝔤)^𝔤 with the Weyl-invariants S(𝔥)^W (Humphreys, *Introduction to Lie Algebras*, §23.1); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: over a nonarchimedean local field with residue field of size q, the totally ramified degree-n extensions inside a separable closure satisfy Σ q^{−c(L)} = n, c(L) the wild exponent (Serre 1978); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: for a number field K, the open finite-index subgroups N of the idele class group correspond bijectively, reversing inclusions, to the finite abelian extensions of K, with C_K/N the Galois group via the Artin map (Milne, *Class Field Theory*, VII Thm 9.5); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: for a nonzero finite module M of finite projective dimension over a Noetherian local ring R, pd M + depth M = depth R (Bruns–Herzog, *Cohen–Macaulay Rings*, Thm 1.3.3); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: the homotopy category H⁰ of twisted objects over any DG category, Bondal–Kapranov's pretriangulated envelope Pre-Tr(C), is a triangulated category (Bondal–Kapranov, *Enhanced triangulated categories*, §1); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: every irreducible rational representation of SL_n(ℂ) is isomorphic to the Weyl module of exactly one Young diagram with at most n − 1 rows (Fulton–Harris, *Representation Theory*, Lecture 15); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: for a finite-dimensional subspace V of the bidual E** and finitely many functionals on E, there is a (1 ± ε)-isomorphism V → E fixing V ∩ E and preserving the values of those functionals (Albiac–Kalton, *Topics in Banach Space Theory*, Thm 12.2.4); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: for a quadratic field K and f ≥ 1, h(O_f) = h_K · f · ∏_{p∣f}(1 − χ_D(p)/p) / [O_K^× : O_f^×] (Cox, *Primes of the Form x² + ny²*, Thm 7.24); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: for a complete Noetherian local ring O with p in its maximal ideal, O⟦T⟧ ≅ lim_n O[ℤ/pⁿ] via T ↦ γ − 1, the finite levels of O⟦ℤ_p⟧ (Washington, *Introduction to Cyclotomic Fields*, Thm 7.1); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: for independent mean-zero random variables Xᵢ ≤ b with Σ E[Xᵢ²] = v, P(Σ Xᵢ ≥ ε) ≤ exp(−ε²/(2(v + bε/3))) (Boucheron–Lugosi–Massart, *Concentration Inequalities*, §2.8); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: a Noetherian local ring is regular exactly when its global dimension is finite, so every localisation of a regular local ring at a prime is again regular (Matsumura, *Commutative Ring Theory*, Thm 19.3); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: a set with the Baire property in X × Y, with Y second countable, is comeagre exactly when comeagrely many of its vertical sections are comeagre (Kechris, *Classical Descriptive Set Theory*, Thm 8.41); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: a local homomorphism from a regular local ring R to a Cohen–Macaulay local ring S with dim S = dim R + dim S/𝔪_R S is flat (Matsumura, *Commutative Ring Theory*, Thm 23.1); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: for n ≥ 1, H^k_dR(Sⁿ) is one-dimensional for k = 0 and k = n and zero in every other degree (Lee, *Introduction to Smooth Manifolds*, Thm 17.21); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: a nilpotent matrix Y lies in the closure of the conjugacy class of a nilpotent X exactly when the Jordan type of X dominates that of Y, for the usual and the Zariski closure (Collingwood–McGovern, *Nilpotent Orbits*, Thm 6.2.5); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: a Banach space E has the approximation property exactly when every compact operator into E is a norm limit of finite-rank operators (Lindenstrauss–Tzafriri, *Classical Banach Spaces I*, Thm 1.e.4); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: every unbounded complex of sheaves of modules on a site receives a quasi-isomorphism from a K-flat complex with flat terms, the companion of the K-injective resolutions announced earlier (Spaltenstein, *Compositio Math.* 65 (1988)); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: a map between standard Borel spaces is Borel exactly when its graph is Borel, equivalently when its graph is analytic; also being formalised in mathlib4#41944 (Kechris, *Classical Descriptive Set Theory*, Thm 14.12); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: a locally BV function u on an open set has a |Du|-a.e. unique unit vector field σ with ∫ u div φ = −∫ ⟨φ, σ⟩ d|Du| for every test field φ (Evans–Gariepy, *Measure Theory and Fine Properties of Functions*, Thm 5.1); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: a finitely generated lattice Λ spanning a vector space over the fraction field of a Dedekind domain equals ⊕ 𝔞ᵢ bᵢ for a basis (bᵢ) and nonzero ideals 𝔞ᵢ (Cohen, *Advanced Topics in Computational Number Theory*, Thm 1.2.25); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: PSL₂(ℤ) is the triangle group Δ(3, 2, ∞) = ⟨x, y, z ∣ x³, y², zyx⟩, that is C₃ ∗ C₂, with x = ST and y = S (Beardon, *The Geometry of Discrete Groups*, §10.6); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: for a homogeneous Markov chain on any measurable state space and a stopping time τ, conditionally on 𝓕_τ and τ < ∞ the path after τ is the chain started at X_τ (Norris, *Markov Chains*, Thm 1.4.2); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: every Banach module over a complete ultrametric ring with discrete value group and field residue ring is continuously isomorphic to a space c₀(I) (Serre, Publ. Math. IHÉS 12 (1962), §1); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: for a homogeneous ideal I and any monomial order, the graded pieces of S/I and of S/in(I) have the same dimension, so I and its initial ideal share a Hilbert function (Cox–Little–O'Shea, *Ideals, Varieties, and Algorithms*, Ch. 9 §3); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: over a field, every ideal of a polynomial ring has exactly one reduced Gröbner basis for a given monomial order (Cox–Little–O'Shea, *Ideals, Varieties, and Algorithms*, Ch. 2 §7 Thm 5); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: for an elimination order, the elements of a Gröbner basis that involve only the retained variables form a Gröbner basis of the elimination ideal (Cox–Little–O'Shea, *Ideals, Varieties, and Algorithms*, Ch. 3 §1 Thm 2); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: a finite graph with more than k vertices is k-connected exactly when any two distinct vertices are joined by k internally disjoint paths; the local form was announced earlier (Diestel, *Graph Theory*, Thm 3.3.6); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: a bounded operator T on the Hardy space H² is the Toeplitz operator of a unique L^∞ symbol exactly when S*TS = T for the shift S (Brown–Halmos, *J. reine angew. Math.* 213 (1964), Thm 6); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: the toric ideal of a : ι → M is generated by the binomials x^u − x^v with Σ uᵢ aᵢ = Σ vᵢ aᵢ, finitely many of them when ι is finite (Sturmfels, *Gröbner Bases and Convex Polytopes*, Lemma 4.1); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: algebra maps out of the Roby algebra Γ^d_R(A) correspond to multiplicative polynomial laws A → B homogeneous of degree d; the linear version was announced earlier (Roby, C. R. Acad. Sci. Paris 290 (1980)); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: K(2√k/(1 + k)) = (1 + k) K(k) for 0 ≤ k < 1, together with Gauss's evaluation K(k) = π/(2 M(1, √(1 − k²))) (Borwein–Borwein, *Pi and the AGM*, Ch. 1); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: every cyclic n-cocycle on an algebra A is the character of an n-dimensional cycle over A, built on the universal forms of A, so cycles and cyclic cocycles correspond (Connes, *Noncommutative Geometry*, III.1 Prop. 4); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: for every group G and G-module A, Hₙ(BG; A) with local coefficients is the group homology Hₙ(G, A); the trivial-coefficient case was announced earlier (Brown, *Cohomology of Groups*, II.4); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: for y^n = f(x) with f squarefree of degree d and n invertible in the constant field, 2g = (n − 1)(d − 2) + n − gcd(n, d) (Stichtenoth, *Algebraic Function Fields and Codes*, Cor. 3.7.4); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: for positive semidefinite matrices ρ, σ, Tr ρ − Tr σ ≤ D(ρ‖σ) = Tr ρ(log ρ − log σ), so the Umegaki relative entropy of density matrices is nonnegative (Nielsen–Chuang, *Quantum Computation and Quantum Information*, Thm 11.7); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: the lemniscate constant satisfies ϖ = π / M(1, √2), with M the arithmetic–geometric mean, and K(1/√2) = Γ(1/4)²/(4√π) (Borwein–Borwein, *Pi and the AGM*, Ch. 1); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: for a derivation D of a commutative ring and a square matrix M, D(det M) = tr(adj(M) · D(M)) (Magnus–Neudecker, *Matrix Differential Calculus*, Ch. 8); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: for a field K with a compatible system of primitive roots of unity of every order, Gal(K⸨X^{1/∞}⸩ / K⸨X⸩) ≅ ℤ̂ as topological groups (Walker, *Algebraic Curves*, Ch. IV); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: a subset of a real normed space is totally bounded exactly when it lies in the closed convex hull of a sequence converging to zero (Lindenstrauss–Tzafriri, *Classical Banach Spaces I*, §1.e); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: every homomorphism from a complex Banach algebra into a commutative semisimple Banach algebra is continuous (Dales, *Banach Algebras and Automatic Continuity*); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: every closed C^r 1-form on a simply connected manifold is the differential of a C^r function, so H¹_dR vanishes (Lee, *Introduction to Smooth Manifolds*, Ch. 11); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: a semisimple Lie subalgebra of 𝔤𝔩(V) over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero contains the semisimple and nilpotent parts of each element, so faithful representations preserve the abstract Jordan decomposition (Humphreys, *Introduction to Lie Algebras*, §6.4); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: s_μ = det(e_{μ′ᵢ − i + j}) in the elementary symmetric polynomials over any commutative ring, the half left open when the Jacobi–Trudi identity was announced (Macdonald, *Symmetric Functions and Hall Polynomials*, I (3.5)); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.
Correctly stated: over every field, in any characteristic, the symplectic transvections generate Sp_{2m}(K) (Artin, *Geometric Algebra*, Ch. III); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: every compact connected abelian Lie group has an element generating a dense subgroup, and such generators form a dense set (Bröcker–tom Dieck, *Representations of Compact Lie Groups*, I.4.14); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: Littelmann's encoding of the LS paths of shape λ by decreasing chains of Weyl-group cosets and rational times satisfying the a-chain condition, finitely many for each λ (Littelmann, *Invent. Math.* 116 (1994)); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: vector fields X with L_X g = 0, characterised by skew-adjointness of ∇X, with ∇²X = R(·, X)· and the restriction of X to any geodesic a Jacobi field (Petersen, *Riemannian Geometry*, Ch. 8); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: the probability laws on ℝ with the stable characteristic function of index α ∈ (0, 2], skewness |β| ≤ 1, scale and location, in Nolan's S₀ parametrisation (Nolan, *Univariate Stable Distributions*, Ch. 1); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: the homology of locally finite singular chains with local coefficients, agreeing with ordinary homology on compact spaces (Bredon, *Sheaf Theory*, Ch. V); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: the group generated by the affine reflections s_{α,k} of a root pairing, whose elements are exactly the affine maps with linear part in W and translation in the coroot lattice, W_aff = Q^∨ ⋊ W (Humphreys, *Reflection Groups and Coxeter Groups*, §4.2); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: Spinᶜ(Q) = (Spin(Q) × U(1))/{±1}, with its determinant map to U(1) and its map to SO(Q), the kernel of their product being of order two (Lawson–Michelsohn, *Spin Geometry*, App. D); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: Serre's π₁(𝔸, T): the free product of the vertex groups and the free group on the edges, modulo the edge relations and the edges of T (Serre, *Trees*, I §5.1); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: the polynomials K_k in the elementary symmetric functions with Σ K_k = ∏ Q(xᵢ) for a power series Q, multiplicative on disjoint unions of roots (Hirzebruch, *Topological Methods in Algebraic Geometry*, §1); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: Z′ = {e : the e-th Z-computable program halts on input e}, with Z <_T Z′ and every Z-c.e. set one-one reducible to Z′ (Soare, *Recursively Enumerable Sets and Degrees*, III.2); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: ϖ = 2∫₀¹ dt/√(1 − t⁴), the half-length of the lemniscate, with the closed form ϖ = Γ(1/4)²/(2√(2π)) (Borwein–Borwein, *Pi and the AGM*, Ch. 1); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated as the real case of the Gelfond–Schneider theorem (real α > 0, real irrational algebraic exponent), as the docstring says; the complex form is not claimed; compared in Voyager's full-statement test.
Correctly stated as the oriented case of the Palais disc theorem (Palais 1960), as the docstring says; compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: the symmetric monoidal structure on modules over a commutative monoid object (Hovey–Shipley–Smith, *Symmetric spectra*, §2.2), closedness not claimed; compared in Voyager's full-statement test.
